risk_assessment.rationale: The email matches the T1566 phishing pattern and carries a generic support-style subject line, but no known malicious IPs or domains are attached. The presence of 23 scanning-related events suggests automated reconnaissance activity.

recommended_actions: Escalate to the incident response / Tier 2 team
recommended_actions_freeform_experimenta: Perform a full content scan of the message body and any attachments using an isolated sandbox environment to detect hidden payloads or obfuscated scripts.

Cross‑reference the sender’s IP (52.14.201.94) against internal whitelists and external threat intelligence feeds; if it appears on any blocklists, add it to the organization’s firewall rules immediately.
Verify the authenticity of the support@printhub-sg.com address by checking DKIM/SPF/DKIM signatures and comparing them with known legitimate records for that domain.
Notify the victimcorp internal security team about the bulk nature of the email and advise users not to click any links or download attachments until a definitive analysis is completed.
If the message contains URLs, resolve each one through a URL reputation service (e.g., Cisco Talos, VirusTotal) and block any that return malicious or suspicious scores.
Log the incident in the SIEM with a dedicated tag for bulk phishing attempts so future correlation can be improved; include the Mimecast review flag as a high‑priority indicator.

Schedule a follow‑up investigation to determine whether this email was part of a larger campaign targeting multiple organizations, using the pattern_type=scanning evidence_count=23 as a trigger for broader threat hunting.
